prompts.title: Active Learning Fit
prompts.text:
The Larner College of Medicine curriculum emphasizes active in-person participation and peer co-learning. This relies on individual students preparing for, and being actively involved in, participatory class sessions. Please share your thoughts on the suitability of active learning for you. Consider the points below to guide your response.

- The value of balancing your learning with the teaching of your classmates.
- Any potential challenges to this approach to learning.
- Personal contributions to such a learning environment and areas of growth.
- Examples of navigating a group learning process such as a flipped classroom experience.

prompts.title: Learning Across Difference
prompts.text: The Larner College of Medicine at the University of Vermont recognizes that diversity extends beyond chosen and unchosen identities and encompasses an individual's entire experiences. Diverse environments can promote growth and provide an opportunity for reflection. Reflect on a time you learned something from someone or a group of people who are unlike yourself and how that challenged your preconceptions or biases. How will this experience influence your behavior in the future?

prompts.title: Professionalism

prompts.title: Why Larner

prompts.title: Regional Medical Campus Interest
prompts.text: If you selected regional medical campus preferred or regional medical campus only, please explain in detail your interest in regional medical campus and how it will be a good fit for your clinical education.

prompts.title: Application Through Matriculation Activities
prompts.text: Please provide the Admissions Committee with a brief summary of your activities, academics, employment or other occupations to account for full-time activity, approximately 30-40 hours per week, from the point of application through matriculation.

prompts.title: Clinical Public Health Interests
prompts.text: The MD Program includes substantial content in Clinical Public Health, including population health, health systems science, health policy, and community health, to prepare GW graduates for an expanded scope of practice required to be successful 21st century physicians. What are your specific interests and experiences related to that aspect of the MD Program?

prompts.title: Uniqueness, Challenges, and Learning
prompts.text: What makes you a unique individual? What challenges have you faced? What have you learned from your experiences?

prompts.title: Specific Interest in GW
prompts.text: What is your specific interest in the MD Program at GW? What opportunities would you take advantage of as a student here? Why?

prompts.title: Prior Admissions Office Interaction
prompts.text: Have you previously interacted directly with the MD Admissions Office through events, tours, fairs, webinars, or interviews? If yes, please explain.

prompts.title: Joint MD MPH Interest
prompts.text: Do you want to pursue the joint MD/MPH program? If yes, please describe why you would want to pursue the MD/MPH program and how the combined degree would fit into your career goals.

why_school_fact: GW is located a few blocks from the White House and pairs public-health/policy proximity with a 17,000+ square-foot Clinical Learning and Simulation Skills Center.
why_school_fact_source: Cached 2027 MSAR profile plus official admissions page listed in this school packet.
estimated_admit_chance_basis: Heuristic, not a true admissions probability. Assumes CA resident, GPA 3.73, MCAT 520, and strong research/service/clinical fit. Uses cached 2027 MSAR-style total applicant/interview/matriculant counts (17194 applied, 746 interviewed, 130 matriculated when available), school medians GPA 3.9 / MCAT 515, private or geography-neutral pool, and research alignment, service alignment, public-health alignment.

estimated_admit_chance_assumptions.profile: California applicant with strong research, clinical exposure, service with vulnerable communities, student advocacy, teaching, leadership, and scientific communication.

name: California Northstate University College of Medicine
secondary_cycle: 2026-2027 live secondary portal prompts provided by applicant on 2026-07-01
notes: Updated from the applicant's California Northstate secondary portal. Portal text did not list a word limit for the pre-health advisor or standardized-tests prompt.

prompts.title: Why CNUCOM
prompts.text: Why have you chosen to apply to CNUCOM?

prompts.title: Diverse Populations and Central Valley
prompts.text: In the medical profession, you will be exposed to students, faculty, colleagues, and patients of various cultures and socioeconomic backgrounds. How has your involvement with diverse populations prepared you for potentially four years in Elk Grove, the greater Sacramento area, and the rest of the Central Valley?

prompts.title: Pre-Health Advisor Experience
prompts.limit: Not listed in portal text provided
prompts.text: Did you have a Pre-Health Advisor at your undergraduate institution? If so, please tell us about your experience. How did it help you in your journey to to apply to medical school? If not, please let us know how you worked independently to find out more about applying to medical school and the path of your journey to apply?

prompts.title: Future Direction of Healthcare
prompts.text: In which direction would you like to see healthcare progress over the next decade?

prompts.title: Education Not Continuous
prompts.text: If your education has not been continuous since high school, please explain why. Examples of discontinuities include time taken off while obtaining your undergraduate degree, in addition to gap years.

prompts.title: Reapplicant Accomplishments
prompts.text: If you have previously applied to medical school, what have you accomplished since that time that would warrant your admission now?

prompts.title: Anything Else
prompts.text: Is there anything you would like the Admissions Committee to know that is not reflected elsewhere in your application?

prompts.title: Standardized Tests and MCAT Preparation
prompts.limit: Not listed in portal text provided
prompts.text: How do you feel about standardized tests? How did you prepare for the MCAT? What tools or preparatory courses/material did you use and how did you study? Do you feel like your score reflects how you will perform in medical school? From what you have learned, do you think it will help you in the way you will study or prepare for USMLE exams?

why_school_fact: California Northstate uses a clinical-presentation-based curriculum and explicitly emphasizes primary care, patient-centeredness, and social accountability in Northern California.
why_school_fact_source: Cached 2027 MSAR profile plus official admissions page listed in this school packet.

Uses cached 2027 MSAR-style res applicant/interview/matriculant counts (2336 applied, 350 interviewed, 109 matriculated when available), school medians GPA 3.89 / MCAT 514, California resident applying in-state, and research alignment, service alignment, community alignment.
